info.title: Volt bridge
info.description:
The wire a Volt bridge serves over a Windows NAMED PIPE — `volt.bridge.<vendor>.<pid>`, one per live IDE. One request object per call: `{ "op": "<name>", "protocol": 1, "body": { ... } }` (a request stating no `protocol` or another is refused PROTOCOL_MISMATCH before its body is read), answered with the method's result or `{ "error": { "code": "...", "message": "...", "data": { ... } } }`.

GENERATED from the C# contract types by `DocDataTests`; edit those, not this file.

servers.name: named-pipe
servers.summary: One pipe per live IDE. Discover by PREFIX — the pid suffix changes when the IDE restarts.

pid.description: The IDE process id the bridge is attached to.

methods.name: health
methods.summary: Liveness plus the connectable projects, from the driver's CACHED snapshot — never marshalled onto the IDE thread. This is the poll path (the connector every few seconds), so it answers while a push or build is running. While paused every row reads idle.
x-outcomes: Never gated by `disconnect` — while paused every row is forced to `idle`, because the list is how the user reconnects.
Answers from the driver's cached snapshot, so it cannot report PLC_DISCONNECTED. A bridge serving nothing is the aggregate status `unavailable` instead.

Answers even when the IDE lacks what the bridge needs: `unsupported` then carries the fixed reason every other op answers with as IDE_UNSUPPORTED, `ideVersion` the IDE version, and every row is idle. Never a version floor — an IDE is refused for what it lacks, not for its number.

Always states the bridge identity at top level, rows or not, refused or not: `productName`, `productVersion` and `productVendor` (what the user runs, its own number and its maker), `ideVersion` (the platform under it — the CODESYS framework version, or the TwinCAT build) and `bridgeVersion` (the stamped release, or `(dev) <commit>` for an unstamped build). Each is absent when its source does not answer, never filled from another, and none of them decides whether the bridge serves.
`ops` names every op this bridge answers, from its own dispatch table: a client asks it before an op an older bridge may lack (`grep`). A frame without `ops` is a bridge from before it.

methods.name: connect
methods.summary: Bind a project and resume service. An absent or empty `project` means "serve whatever you have". Refuses with PLC_DISCONNECTED unless the bridge ends up actually serving the named project — the post-condition is enforced in shared code, so both vendors answer identically.
x-outcomes: PLC_DISCONNECTED here is the POST-condition: the driver attached nothing, or attached something other than the project named. Enforced once in shared code, so both vendors refuse identically.
A REFUSED connect still leaves the bridge RESUMED: the pause flag is cleared before the IDE work, so a `disconnect` racing a connect wins.

methods.name: disconnect
methods.summary: Pause the bridge: refuse sync until the next connect, tear nothing down. Answers even while a push is running, and that push RUNS TO COMPLETION — the gate stops the NEXT op, never the current one.
x-outcomes: Fails only with IDE_UNSUPPORTED, as every op but `health` does on an IDE the bridge cannot serve. Otherwise it sets a flag and answers. It is deliberately not marshalled onto the IDE thread, so it answers even while a push is running — and that push runs to completion. The gate stops the NEXT op, never the current one.

methods.name: refs
methods.summary: The version map without any content: every tracked item's version, its folder, and the aggregate project/structure versions. This is what a client compares against to decide what to fetch.
x-outcomes: ITEM_UNVERIFIED as an error FRAME (TwinCAT): the Solution Explorer hierarchy cannot vouch for the PLC project ITSELF (DIALECT C2i), so the walk stops before anything is read. Fix what stops the IDE enumerating it.
An item whose body will not materialize is NOT an error: it is named in `unreadable`, keeps a stable sentinel version so a pull does not mistake it for deleted, and is logged at Warn.
A read is retried ONCE through a transient IDE failure that the driver classifies as one. The session is marked degraded meanwhile, which `health` reports.

Progress frames start with the WALK: one per application as the walk finishes it, `phase: "walking"`, `done` applications of `total` (a TwinCAT PLC project is an application; CODESYS states no `total`). The item frames follow: `phase: "reading"` with `done` 0 of `total` items, then one every 25 items and one at the last.

A `refs` that arrives while one with the same body runs JOINS it: it receives that one's progress frames from then on and the same terminal frame, result or error. Nothing is kept once it answers: the next `refs` walks again.

methods.name: fetch
methods.summary: Item CONTENT. `knownItems` narrows the answer to what changed; `onlyItems` restricts the walk to a named subset. Naming a `.library` returns its manifest and every signature of that library, in the folder and with the bytes a full fetch writes; the first such read of a session pays the vendor's extraction (on CODESYS a build of the application, which writes the IDE's message view), later ones with no library change reuse it, and `libraryManifestOnly` answers the manifest alone. A directed read never sets `librariesRefreshed`. Graphical bodies arrive as network text — the bridge materializes them, so a client never sees a vendor's own form.
x-outcomes: ITEM_UNVERIFIED as an error FRAME (TwinCAT): the Solution Explorer hierarchy cannot vouch for the PLC project ITSELF (DIALECT C2i), so the walk stops before anything is read. Fix what stops the IDE enumerating it.

BAD_REQUEST for a fetch with neither `knownItems` nor `onlyItems` nor `init: true`: it is ambiguous — it could mean "everything" or a client that forgot its baseline. Send `init: true` for a first pull. (It was NO_SIDECAR, a code named after a cache no client sees.)
A walk that could not enumerate a folder reports no deletion beneath it and says so at Warn; a known path absent from a folder it did read (the path's own prefix) is still in `removed`.
Items that would not materialize are named in `unreadable`, not raised.

Progress frames start with the WALK: one per application as the walk finishes it, `phase: "walking"`, `done` applications of `total` (a TwinCAT PLC project is an application; CODESYS states no `total`). The item frames follow: `phase: "reading"` with `done` 0 of `total` items, then one every 25 items and one at the last.

methods.name: push
methods.summary: Apply ops to the IDE. Every text-decidable refusal runs in a PRE-FLIGHT before the first write, so a push that cannot land in full lands nothing. `expectedProjectVersion` is the lease; per-item `ifVersion` is the optimistic guard.
x-outcomes: ITEM_UNVERIFIED as an error FRAME (TwinCAT): the Solution Explorer hierarchy cannot vouch for the PLC project ITSELF (DIALECT C2i), so the walk stops before anything is read. Fix what stops the IDE enumerating it.

IDE_BUSY as an error FRAME when another push or build holds the IDE: one gate, tried before the op is marshalled and never waited on, so nothing is applied or compiled. Both vendors answer it alike (CODESYS used to run the op nested inside the running build). Reads and `health` are not gated. Wait for the running op, then try once.

BAD_REQUEST as an error FRAME when `expectedPlatform` or `expectedProjectName` is absent or empty, naming each missing member, before anything is walked: a write names the project it writes. The reads keep both optional.
A push writes into the open project and saves nothing, on both vendors: the engineer saves.
MOST PUSH FAILURES ARE NOT ERROR FRAMES. Every exception from the pre-flight and from the apply loop is caught and returned as a conflict. A client MUST check `accepted` AND `conflicts`.

A refusal carries its CODE on the conflict: a `NETWORK_*` diagnostic for a body the format refuses (with a `line`), or a BridgeErrorCodes value for everything else — UNSUPPORTED, IDE_LOST_ITEM, DUPLICATE_CHILD, BAD_REQUEST, INVALID_ST, UNREADABLE, and INTERNAL_ERROR for a refusal nobody coded. Match the code, never the message.
A version conflict is also `accepted:false` — with `yourVersion`/`currentVersion` per item.
A refusal decidable before the first write writes nothing and names EVERY refused op — the gate's per-item conflicts and the pre-flight's, one conflict per op.

A refusal during APPLY leaves the earlier ops WRITTEN, not rolled back, and stops the push: it is `accepted:true` with the receipt and a conflict per op NOT landed — the refused op with its code, every later op NOT_ATTEMPTED. Every op the conflicts do not name landed.

What of the REFUSED op itself the IDE kept is in fields as well as in `reason`: `partiallyApplied: true` whenever any of it stays (re-read the item before retrying it), `renamedTo` with the item's current full name after a native rename that ran first, `remains: true` for a create whose rollback failed. Each is ABSENT when it does not apply — never false.

methods.name: build
methods.summary: Compile the bound project and return the IDE's own diagnostics. This is the oracle a client uses to tell its own analysis from the vendor's.
x-outcomes: IDE_BUSY as an error FRAME when another push or build holds the IDE: one gate, tried before the op is marshalled and never waited on, so nothing is applied or compiled. Both vendors answer it alike (CODESYS used to run the op nested inside the running build). Reads and `health` are not gated. Wait for the running op, then try once.

BAD_REQUEST as an error FRAME when `expectedPlatform` or `expectedProjectName` is absent or empty, naming each missing member, before anything is walked: a write names the project it writes. The reads keep both optional.

BAD_REQUEST for an `applications` root the project does not hold (named), or an empty list, before anything is built. Named roots build those applications alone and report only their diagnostics; absent, every application is built.
The guard sits OUTSIDE the try, deliberately — otherwise WRONG_PROJECT would be swallowed into a fake "build failed" diagnostic instead of surfacing as an error frame.
Everything after it IS caught: a thrown build answers `success:false` with the message as one error-severity diagnostic. So this op essentially never returns INTERNAL_ERROR.
The build compiles what the IDE holds in memory, and Volt calls no save. On TwinCAT a build saves changed documents, as XAE's Build does (DIALECT D45).
`success` comes from a different vendor SIGNAL on each: CODESYS derives it from the diagnostics, TwinCAT reads the IDE's own count of failed projects.

methods.name: grep
methods.summary: Search the text `fetch` ships for each item, line by line, and answer the matching LINES — path, 1-based line, the line as fetched — with each matched item's `refs` version, never whole sources. A regular expression or `literal` text, ignoring case unless `caseSensitive`; `paths` globs limit what is searched. What could not be searched is named in `notSearched`.
x-outcomes: ITEM_UNVERIFIED as an error FRAME (TwinCAT): the Solution Explorer hierarchy cannot vouch for the PLC project ITSELF (DIALECT C2i), so the walk stops before anything is read. Fix what stops the IDE enumerating it.

BAD_REQUEST, before the walk, for an empty `pattern`, a regular expression that does not compile (the parse error named) or a `limit` outside 1–1000; and, with no partial answer, for a pattern that takes longer than 100 ms on one line.

What it searches is what `fetch` ships as text, from the same walk: a matched line is the fetched line at that number, byte for byte. An `unreadable` item, and a body that reads `IMPLEMENTATION <LANG> UNSUPPORTED`, are named in `notSearched` instead; libraries are out of scope and unlisted.
The answer is bounded: at most `limit` matches, counted up to 10000 in `totalMatches`; `truncated` when more were found than answered.

op.description: Selects which member of the union this object is.
